figures.caption: Figure 1: Performance Evaluation on Synthetic EEG Datasets. (a) Characterization of Synthetic Datasets: The upper (middle) panels display the group-specific Power Spectral Density (PSD), averaged across channels and subjects within the validation partition for the α (β/γ) datasets. The lower panels show representative 2-second EEG segments for the three simulated midline channels across both datasets. (b) Reconstruction Fidelity across Latent Dimensions: Model performance is reported as 1 − MSE (where 1 indicates perfect reconstruction) on the held-out test partition. Results are shown for the LSTMVAE (upper), VAEEG (middle), and Transformer (lower) architectures as a function of the latent space dimensionality (NLS) and dataset type. (c) Latent Space Discriminative Power: Classification accuracy on the held-out test partition of a non-linear MLP trained to predict diagnostic group (HC, SCD, MCI, AD) from the latent embeddings. Accuracy is reported for the LSTMVAE, VAEEG, Transformer, and REVE (top to bottom), across varying latent dimensions. (d) provides a detail-view of REVE’s high accuracy. Theoretical chance accuracy (25%) is denoted by the horizontal red dashed line. Error bars indicate 95% confidence interval.

Figure 2: UMAP Projections of Latent Space Embeddings (NLS = 50). Two-dimensional UMAP visualizations of the latent manifolds learned by the LSTMVAE (left), VAEEG (middle), and Transformer (right) architectures. The upper row displays projections for the α slowing dataset, while the lower row represents the β/γ slowing dataset. Each point corresponds to a multi-channel EEG segment from the held-out test partition, color-coded by the synthetic diagnostic group (HC, SCD, MCI, AD) to illustrate the degree of class-wise clustering and separability within the learned latent space.

Figure 4: Spectral Organization of the LSTMVAE Latent Space for the held-out test partition of the BBHI Dataset. (a) UMAP projections of the latent embeddings color-coded by the grand-average (average over all channels) relative power within standard EEG frequency bands: theta (4− 8 Hz), alpha (8− 13 Hz), and beta (13− 30 Hz). (b) Topographically resolved UMAP projections of alpha relative band power for the LSTMVAE (upper) and REVE (lower) models. Color-coding alpha band power is the result of averaging alpha band power over different sets of channels: Frontal (F7, F3, Fz, F4, F8), Temporal (T7, T8), and Central (C3, Cz, C4). These projections aim to illustrate the emergence of spectral and spatial representational structure within the unsupervised latent manifold.

Figure 5: Frequency-resolved spectral decay across reconstruction autoencoders as a function of latent space dimension (NLS), evaluated on the held-out test partition of the BBHI dataset. Power spectral densities (PSDs) of target 2-second EEG windows from the BBHI dataset (black) are compared against the PSDs of reconstructed outputs for the LSTMVAE (top, red gradient), VAEEG (middle, blue gradient), and Transformer (bottom, green gradient) models. Three latent space dimensions are shown, NLS = {50, 250, 500}, with color intensity increasing from lighter to darker shades as NLS increases. Higher NLS improves high-frequency reconstruction fidelity, particularly for the Transformer architecture.

Figure 6: UMAP Projections of Latent Space Embeddings (NLS = 250). Two-dimensional UMAP visualizations of the latent manifolds learned by the (left to right) LSTMVAE, VAEEG, Transformer, and REVE architectures. The upper row displays projections for the α slowing dataset, while the lower row represents the β/γ slowing dataset. Each point corresponds to a multi-channel EEG segment from the held-out test partition, color-coded by the synthetic diagnostic group (HC, SCD, MCI, AD) to illustrate the degree of class-wise clustering and separability within the learned latent space.

Figure 7: Spectral Learning Order - Reconstruction Examples Evolution of reconstructed segments in the synthetic experiment adapted from Rahaman et al. [36] illustrating the evolution of frequency learning as a function of training progress in the equal-amplitude condition (Ai = 1) across three architectures: LSTMVAE (upper panels), VAEEG (middle panels), and Transformer (lower panels), all with NLS = 50
Figure 8: UMAP projection of LS embeddings for LSTMVAE NLS = 50, coloured by demographic information (sex, age, and cognitive performance measured with MMSE)
Figure 9: UMAP projection of LS embeddings for REVE BaseNLS = 512, coloured by demographic information (sex, age, and cognitive performance measured with MMSE)
Figure 10: Spectral Learning Order Study on REVE. For Figure details, refer to Figure 3 in the manuscript.
Figure 11: Spectral Learning Order Study on LSTMVAE and Transformer reconstruction autoencoders with a modified masked autoencoding objective. For Figure details, refer to Figure 3 in the manuscript.

Figure 12: Topographical Mapping of Spectral Decay in the held-out test partition of the BBHI Dataset for LSTMVAE (upper left), VAEEG (upper right), and Transformer (lower). Regional distribution of band-specific spectral attenuation (∆PdB) as a function of increasing latent space dimensionality (NLS). Results are shown for the delta, theta, alpha, beta, and gamma bands across the scalp. Lighter hues indicate minimized attenuation (higher reconstruction fidelity), whereas darker hues denote regions of significant power loss, highlighting the spatial and spectral dependencies of the LSTMVAE. reconstruction process.
